problem_statement: The paper frames portfolio optimization as selecting a subset of assets under a budget constraint so that risk is minimized and return is maximized. It presents this as a combinatorial optimization problem over binary decision variables.
problem_statement_quotes: As a ﬁrst computational illustration of WS-QAOA, we solve combinatorial-optimization problems framed as a ﬁnancial-portfolio optimization with a budget con- straint [15].
An optimal portfolio minimizes risk and maximizes return by exploiting imperfect correlations in a covariance matrix Σ between n assets with ex- pected returns µ [86].

classical_baseline: The paper treats continuous relaxations of the binary portfolio problem as the classical baseline, especially the convex quadratic relaxation when it applies. It also notes that such relaxations can be solved efficiently with classical optimizers, and that classical solvers like CPLEX are used to obtain the relaxed solution.
classical_baseline_quotes: Classical solvers for such problems employ relax- ations, which replace binary variables with continuous ones,
classical_difficulty: The paper says the underlying binary optimization is NP-hard, and that even checking local optimality is NP-hard. It also emphasizes that more general relaxations can become super-polynomial or require many qubits if represented directly, which limits classical or near-term tractability in some settings.
classical_difficulty_quotes: Considering that any mixed-integer linear program can be encoded in a QUBO [60], QUBO is NP-Hard.
Indeed, even checking local optimality is NP-Hard [61], and hence only very special cases [62, 63] can be solved in polynomial time.

However, higher-order relaxations within these hierarchies [72–74] require a run-time of the classical SDP solver which is super-polynomial in the number n of integral decision variables in (QUBO) and the order in the hi- erarchy [72–74].
extraction_notes: Motivation is explicit in the portfolio-optimization section; business stakes are not discussed beyond generic risk/return language.
